status: fitted_to_literature_anchors; not yet used in any frozen simulation batch

gprmax_semantics.debye_pole: epsilon(f) = epsilon_inf + sum_i dE_i / (1 + j*2*pi*f*tau_i); verified against gprMax 4.0.0 user_objects/cmds_multiuse.py AddDebyeDispersion docstring (er_delta = static minus infinite per pole, tau in seconds)
gprmax_semantics.cole_cole_note: gprMax 4.0.0 has no Cole-Cole; the 20 MHz low-end rise of real wet clay is underfit by Debye poles (documented residual)

fit_quality.method: scipy least_squares TRF, 30 restarts, joint fit of 7 epsilon' and 7 sigma_eff anchors; 1-pole Debye preferred (2/3-pole fits degenerate to 1 pole)
fit_quality.systematic_note: fitted band-center epsilon' is ~2 units above the archived constant-er=16 model; dispersive runs are a new variant family, archived non-dispersive results stay valid for what they certified

anchors_basis: West et al. 2003 (WRR 39, doi:10.1029/2001WR000923): clay-rich saturated sandstone Kr 25-30 @75 MHz falling to 15-18 above 350 MHz; Maxwell-Wagner characteristic frequency ~100 MHz at groundwater salinity; sand+bentonite mixtures much stronger (Kr 30-60 @100 MHz)
Ishida et al. 2000 (via West 2003): saturated montmorillonite Kr 175 @10 MHz -> 75 @100 MHz (upper-bound dispersion, pure clay)
Gonzalez-Teruel et al. 2022 (Comput. Electron. Agric. 195:106847): clay loam/silt dispersion concentrated below 300 MHz, grows with water content
anchor epsilon'(20 MHz)=28 chosen between the sandstone-mixture trend and the pure-montmorillonite extreme; it is the least certain anchor (marked, not a measurement of our site)

transition_zone.basis: design assumption: cover/rock mixture, half-strength pole at the same relaxation frequency; no direct measurement

bedrock_sandstone.basis: West et al. 2003: clay-poor medium-grained sandstone shows only mild dispersion in 50-200 MHz; our bedrock (er=9, sigma=0.001) is less conductive than their saturated samples, i.e. partially saturated, where dispersion is weaker still. Keep non-dispersive; revisit if site data show clay-rich bedrock.

validity_limits: anchors are literature consensus for wet silty clay / clay-bearing sandstone, not measurements of the project site; site borehole/lab calibration would supersede
Peplinski-style soil mixing models are rated 0.3-1.3 GHz and were NOT used (out of band), per AGENTS.md standing note
sigma_eff inside 20-170 MHz is 0.007-0.014 S/m for cover clay (vs 0.01 constant before); DC conductivity alone no longer defines loss
temperature assumed ~20 C; no temperature correction applied
